### msk-acl-default-allow-everyone-if-no-acl-found

**Claim.** Amazon MSK sets allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found to true by default, so if you do not set ACLs on a resource all principals can access it, and if you enable ACLs on a resource only the authorized principals can access it.

**Write it as.** `Amazon MSK sets it to true by default` · `only the authorized principals can access it`

**Scope.** per MSK cluster, Kafka ACL authorizer; default; adjustable.

> "To change this Apache Kafka behavior, you set the property `allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found` to true. Amazon MSK sets it to true by default. This means that with Amazon MSK clusters, if you don't explicitly set ACLs on a resource, all principals can access this resource. If you enable ACLs on a resource, only the authorized principals can access it."
> — [Apache Kafka ACLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/msk/latest/developerguide/msk-acls.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### msk-api-interface-endpoint-privatelink

**Claim.** An interface VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink keeps traffic between your VPC and the Amazon MSK APIs inside the Amazon network, with no internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection or AWS Direct Connect connection needed. It covers the MSK Provisioned and MSK Connect APIs.

**Write it as.** `Interface VPC Endpoint, powered by AWS PrivateLink` · `don't require an internet gateway`

**Scope.** MSK APIs (control plane).

> "You can use an Interface VPC Endpoint, powered by AWS PrivateLink, to prevent traffic between your Amazon VPC and Amazon MSK APIs from leaving the Amazon network. Interface VPC Endpoints don't require an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or AWS Direct Connect connection."

### msk-auto-recovery-replaces-failed-broker

> "When Amazon MSK detects a broker failure, it mitigates the failure or replaces the unhealthy or unreachable broker with a new one. In addition, where possible, it reuses the storage from the older broker to reduce the data that Apache Kafka needs to replicate."
